= oracle_demo: the fixture library of an oracle
:toc: left
:toclevels: 2
:idprefix:
:sectanchors:

oracle_demo ports two functions of JavaScript to {cpp}, which the tests of its
build place in `libs/oracle_demo` of a scratch superproject.

Of its {n-examples} examples, {n-examples-with-original} have a twin, the same
program in JavaScript: {n-twins-agreeing} prints what its example prints, and
{n-twins-divergent} prints an output of its own. {n-examples-without-twin} has
no twin.

[#square]
== Square

A program squares a number:

[source]
----
include::{examples}/square.cpp[lines=11..-1]
----

It prints what its twin prints:

[source,javascript]
----
include::{twins}/square.mjs[lines=9..-1]
----

[listing]
----
include::{examples}/square.expected[]
----

[#half]
== Half

A program halves a number, rounding toward zero:

[source]
----
include::{examples}/half.cpp[lines=11..-1]
----

[listing]
----
include::{examples}/half.expected[]
----

Its twin keeps the fraction, which JavaScript's division does not drop:

[listing]
----
include::{twins}/half.expected[]
----

[#compile-time]
== At compile time

A program squares a number before it runs, which JavaScript cannot:

[source]
----
include::{examples}/compile_time.cpp[lines=11..-1]
----
